To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the performance of computer vision algorithms is highly dependent on hyperparameters; (b) the best hyperparameter values for a given data set are not always obvious; (c) the best hyperparameters for a given algorithm are not always the same across data sets; and (d) a meta-modeling framework can be used to automate the process of finding the best hyperparameters.
we can optimize vision architecture hyperparameters using a single meta-model, and that this meta-model is effective for a range of tasks.

(a) a meta-modeling framework for automated hyperparameter optimization of machine learning algorithms can be constructed, (b) this framework can yield significant improvements in performance on a range of computer vision tasks, and (c) this framework is sufficiently general to be applicable to a wide range of vision architectures and problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
making a science of model search.
making the process of model search more scientific.
making the search for the best model architecture a science, not an art.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have shown how to automatically tune the hyperparameters of vision architectures in hundreds of dimensions, and we have shown how our approach can yield results that compare favorably with the state of the art on three disparate problems.
we present a new method for hyperparameter optimization that is effective in hundreds of dimensions, and that is applicable to many vision architectures.

our approach yields a state of the art result on the LFW face matching problem, while yielding results comparable to the state of the art on both the PubFig83 face identification and CIFAR-10 object recognition tasks.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of hyperparameter optimization is not a separate problem from the task of algorithm design, and that the two problems should be considered together.
